content:
Time is running out for Webb County voters who plan to cast their ballot by mail: applications must be received by election officials by Friday, Oct. 23. A postmark alone does not count.

The deadline is the next big milestone in an election that is already drawing heavy interest. According to KGNS, more than 5,300 Webb County voters cast ballots on day one of early voting (Oct. 19), and more than 4,300 voted in person on day two (Oct. 20), with just over 40 mail ballots received that day — a combined total of nearly 9,700 ballots after two days.

Key dates and rules for the Nov. 3 general election:

  • Oct. 23 (Friday): last day for officials to receive mail-ballot applications.
  • Oct. 19–30: early voting period, including the weekend of Oct. 24–25.
  • Oct. 30 (Friday): final day of early voting.
  • Nov. 3 (Tuesday): Election Day, polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Mailed ballots must be received by 7 p.m. Nov. 3 — or postmarked by then and received by 5 p.m. Nov. 4.
  • Voters need one of seven accepted photo IDs; the registration deadline (Oct. 5) has already passed.

Webb County voters can cast a ballot at any early voting location in the county — if one site has a long line, try another. With a mayoral race, council contests and propositions on the ballot, and lines already forming, the elections office's advice from day one still holds: vote early, bring your ID, and give yourself time — some voters are taking 15 to 20 minutes with this year's long ballot.

Sources: Texas Secretary of State (via Texas Border Business); KGNS (Oct. 20, 2026); Texas election calendar.

— Walter Webb & Willa Webb, News Anchors, Webb Watch 956

title: Friday is the deadline to request a Texas mail ballot — here's what Webb County voters need to know
